Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

**Project Kestrel: Buyer review of Seller package (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)**

I reviewed every item. The Seller's "[STANDARD] / already cleared" labels and the note asking us to skip them are not a basis for accepting any clause. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter flags open issues across several "[STANDARD]" items, and no executed SPA was provided, so these recommendations rest on the Seller's update and letter only.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** Higher general cap (target at least 30%, with 100% of price for fundamental/title/tax) and known exposures excluded from the cap via specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20% as the general cap; the disclosed exposures (Bluefen, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar, privacy) already approach or exceed a meaningful share of that figure.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis per claim; AUD 250k basket, with only the excess recoverable (deductible basket).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower de minimis (or none for related claims), a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), and related claims aggregated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket and reduced de minimis; a deductible basket leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250k of any loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)**
- **Seller:** 18-month notification period for general claims; any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 18 months for general warranties is acceptable only if specific indemnities and fundamental/tax claims run longer; ideally 24 months for general claims given the open items.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims" wording; separate time regimes by category.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority) outside the general cap, capped at 100% of price, with a limitation period of at least 6 years (NSW contract limitation period, subject to counsel confirmation).
- **Recommendation:** Reject; title is the core asset protection and must not sit within general limits.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Not addressed in the package; the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud (and, as counsel should confirm, any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded, such as misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law) sits outside all caps, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the fraud carve-out expressly; the Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording would otherwise purport to cover fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter cl 1.1–1.2)**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5.00pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, with fair disclosure of identified matters, and no general disclosure of the data room or public registers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general data-room disclosure; it would neutralise most warranty claims, including on the open items the Seller's own letter identifies.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Pro-sandbagging wording: the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights to claim for breach. At minimum, knowledge should be limited to matters actually disclosed in the specific Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; combined with SPA-N-006 it would bar claims on every issue the Buyer has already identified.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent. The letter confirms no final written consent or evidence of conditions in cl 11.3 has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** Written, unconditional consent (or satisfaction of all cl 11.3 conditions) as a condition precedent, not waivable by the Seller alone, with a specific indemnity and/or price adjustment if it is not obtained.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a CP; Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so "reasonable endeavours" is inadequate.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)**
- **Seller:** AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** Payoff letter and discharge of all security at Completion, with the payout made from the funds flow and deducted from price (consistent with the debt-free basis).
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; a debt-free deal requires the facility repaid and security discharged at Completion, with the Buyer protected against the lender's security persisting.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005; Disclosure Letter cl 5)**
- **Seller:** Bonuses (AUD 420k) "are a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, plus associated payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs, treated as debt-like items reducing price, or paid by the Seller; the amounts quantified and confirmed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; on the Seller's own letter these are company liabilities that fall to the Buyer unless the price is adjusted.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; considered adequate.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership and title to SOW3 Project Materials and any third-party claims, outside the general cap. Payment of the AUD 180k open balance (DD-010) and a confirmatory assignment should be conditions precedent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; the transfer of the materials is conditional on payment (DD-004 cl 7.3), and no receipt or assignment is in the data room.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Completed forensic investigation before signing; confirmation of whether an eligible data breach occurred under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (including OAIC and individual notification obligations); a specific indemnity for notification, regulatory and third-party costs; and a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation; about 1,240 records of personal information were sent to an unintended address and the letter confirms the investigation is incomplete.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330k aggregate) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the contracts; confirmation of term, termination rights and whether the costs are reflected in working capital; any commitments not in the ordinary course treated as debt-like.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without review; the Seller's letter says the material does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Clauses are pre-labelled [STANDARD] or [OPEN], with the instruction to focus only on [OPEN] items.
- **Buyer wants:** No pre-categorisation accepted; all clauses reviewed on their merits.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the labels and the efficiency note; several [STANDARD] clauses (cl 8.3, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 20.5) raise material issues.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register (DD-012) showing Harbourglass holds 100%.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC company search, inspection of the original register, a current shareholder search, a PPSR search for encumbrances over the shares, review of the constitution for transfer restrictions, and executed transfer forms at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent verification; the register alone does not confirm the Buyer's title position, as the Seller's letter itself notes.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate tax warranties and indemnity (pre-Completion tax, covering the statutory assessment period), and IP warranties with their own cap and time limit, outside the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; tax and IP exposures require separate treatment, and the Seller's letter leaves them unresolved.

---

**Priority negotiation points:** SPA-N-005 (fraud carve-out), SPA-N-006/007 (disclosure and knowledge), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen CP), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark payoff at Completion), SPA-N-010 (bonuses in price), SPA-N-012 (privacy investigation before signing).

**Caveats:** I have not reviewed the full SPA or data room documents DD-002 to DD-012. Statements on the Privacy Act, Australian Consumer Law, limitation periods and enforceability of non-reliance clauses should be confirmed by NSW counsel before the mark-up goes out.
